newsitem.title: EGYPT: SOCCER-FANCIED TEAMS HAVE EASY ROUTES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FANCIED TEAMS HAVE EASY ROUTES.

text.p: All of the fancied teams for next year's African Champions' Cup title were handed relatively easy routes into the final eight when the draw was released by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) in Cairo on Thursday.

Egypt's Zamalek, who seek a record fourth Champions' Cup title on Friday night when they meet Nigeria's Shooting Stars in the second leg of this year's final, will lead the chase for next year's title, even if they lose to the Nigerians.
Zamalek open their campaign next year against St George of Ethiopia and then, if they progress as expected, are likely to play against Zambian champions Mufulira Wanderers.
Other former winners Mouloudia Alger of Algeria, Morocco's Raja Casablanca and the Tunisians Club Africain will also have easy opposition as they seek a place in the final eight.
They should be joined by Kaizer Chiefs of South Africa, Goldfields of Ghana and Ivorian champions Africa Sports in the new African Champions' League in September.

The eight quarter-finalists will be divided into two groups of four for the format of the new competition, to be played on a home and away league basis, with the group winners going through to the final.
The African Champions' League will be launched in September.

Thursday's draw is dependant on Zamalek winning the Champions' Cup final on Friday. If Shooting Stars hold on to their 2-1 first leg lead then a revised draw will be released with the Nigerian team included as well.
In the Cup Winners' Cup, holders Arab Contractors open the defence of their title against Kenya's Mumias Sugar FC.
Contractors won the trophy last Friday with a 4-0 aggregate win in Cairo over Zaire's Sodigraf.
Defending CAF Cup champions Kawkab Marrakesh meet ASC Linguere of Senegal in their first round tie.
The three African club competitions kick off on of January 31, February 1 and 2 with preliminary round matches.
First round matches will be played in March and second round games scheduled for May.
